A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BHyT research work. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support comparison. Changed experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons but do not prevent reliable assessment of the revision.

before.justification: v2 reports original Llama-1B and Llama-3B pretraining, fine-tuning, activation-statistics, and timing results in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v3 reports original pretraining and fine-tuning results across 374M, 1B, and 3B models, alongside residual-stack simulations and efficiency measurements in Section 4 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core BHyT transformation, block algorithm, and attention-output variance approximation remain intact. Appendix C.11 adds a tested hybrid variant that computes exact variance in the first two layers before using the standard approximation, a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v3 adds harder ARC-C question answering, CommonSenseQA validation for checkpoint selection, and WikiText-2 language-model evaluation outside the C4 corpus. C4, Lima1K, and the original seven downstream benchmarks remain, so coverage expands within the existing English-language domain.

E2.justification: The existing Llama-1B 20B-token comparison expands from Peri-LN alone against BHyT in v2 Table 11 to RMSNorm, Peri-LN, LNS, and DyT in v3 Tables 1–2. This substantially broadens the long-budget comparison. The short-budget 3B comparator set remains in v3 Appendix C.5.

E3.justification: The main evaluation shifts from short-budget 1B/3B experiments to 374M trained on 7.5B tokens and full-baseline 1B experiments on 20B tokens, with 3-shot rather than 5-shot evaluation. Figure 3 replaces the fixed-learning-rate, 20K-step diagnostic with selected hyperparameters and 20B-token training. New toy-stack and component-latency experiments introduce additional controlled protocols.

E4.justification: v3 adds controlled residual-stack tests of output magnitude and DyT scaling, an early-layer exact-variance hybrid analysis, normalization-only latency comparisons, and post-SFT forgetting/generalization checks. Learning-rate sensitivity, time-to-target-loss analysis, and Table 5's approximation ablation are retained. Variance-approximation plots are revised, while v2's aggregate fit-quality table is removed.

E5.justification: v3 specifies one pretraining run with five prompt-sampling seeds for its new main results and separately describes five SFT seeds; v2's five-training-seed 3B results remain in Appendix C.5. It adds timing-batch repetition details without establishing an increase beyond five repeats, and removes the uncertainty-bearing approximation summary from v2 Table 7.

E6.justification: v3 adds 374M results, expanded 20B-token comparisons, post-SFT perplexities, and component-latency measurements, while revising activation and generation results. For example, reported BHyT throughput at 512 output tokens changes from 39.4 to 1199.9 tokens/s; insufficiently matched measurement settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting speedup. The short-budget 3B tables and Table 5 ablation retain their numerical contents.

T1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds a deterministic Jacobian-norm comparison with RMSNorm and its chain-rule derivation. The existing input-bounding, attention/MLP variance, and finite-depth proofs are retained. The depth example is also corrected from approximately 100 layers to the strict condition L < 100.

C1.justification: The abstract substantially reduces the claimed average training advantage over RMSNorm from 15.8% to 1.6%, and generation advantage from 4.2% to 1.77%, alongside revised evaluations. The contribution narrative now emphasizes a modest stability–efficiency trade-off and strong pretraining/post-SFT performance. The central BHyT proposal remains unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 expands the DyT explanation by connecting residual growth to sublayer-output magnitude and distinguishing bounded outputs from controlled residual accumulation. It newly discusses accumulated approximation error and the importance of early layers, explicitly limits the toy study to a non-Transformer stack, and interprets post-SFT perplexity as evidence about forgetting and generalization.

D1.justification: v3 supplies additional SFT epoch/checkpoint-selection details and generation settings, including GPU, fp16, batch size, decoding, caching, and warmup/timed batches. It clarifies periodic approximation-term refresh and replaces the anonymous code address with a named GitHub repository link. Most existing hyperparameter and training-hardware disclosures remain unchanged; newly supplied details do not establish corresponding changes to earlier runs.

R1.justification: v3 adds a focused comparison with concurrent Derf and SeeDNorm work, plus references supporting compute-optimal budgets and new evaluation datasets. These concurrent methods are discussed rather than experimentally evaluated. The updated publication information for the curse-of-depth paper represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methodology explanations, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Section 4 is reorganized around protocols, stability, performance, and efficiency, while retained experimental material is redistributed into Appendix C, replacing the earlier separate D–E organization.

P2.justification: Figures 2–4 are substantially revised, including correlation annotations and a throughput bar chart replacing per-layer timing curves. Main tables are restructured for multiple model scales and additional metrics; legacy 3B tables move to the appendix. v3 also adds the toy-stack figure and baseline-formulation/component-latency tables and removes the aggregate approximation-quality table.

improvement.justification: The full-baseline 20B-token comparison, post-SFT language-model checks, and clearer protocols strengthen evidence beyond v2's restricted long-budget comparisons. Targeted mechanism and latency analyses also help explain the method. These benefits are tempered by removed aggregate approximation validation and new reporting errors: Table 3 supports accuracy margins of 2.78 and 2.21 points rather than 3.4 and 2.5, and Figure 4 identifies the cited 83K tokens/s as forward-only throughput. The net quality gain is positive but limited.
